exams.summary: Analogies, vocabulary, grammar, short passages, quantitative problems and logical deduction.
exams.source: Practice paper compiled from the NGAT PDFs in assets. Items that depended on a missing chart or diagram were left out.

questions.stem: SEGREGATE : UNIFY :: repair :
questions.explanation: Segregate is the opposite of unify. Repair is the opposite of damage.

questions.stem: monarch : ______ :: KING : COBRA
questions.explanation: A king cobra is a kind of snake named with “king”. A monarch butterfly is the matching pair, so the missing word is butterfly.

questions.stem: EXECUTIONER : CRIMINAL
questions.explanation: An executioner performs his work on a criminal. A butcher performs his work on an animal.

questions.stem: LOATH : COERCION
questions.explanation: To be loath is to be unwilling, and coercion is forcing someone. Reluctant is the matching attitude toward persuasion.

questions.stem: MOON : SATELLITE
questions.explanation: The Moon is an example of a satellite. Earth is an example of a planet.

questions.stem: POETRY : RHYME :: philosophy :
questions.explanation: Rhyme is a characteristic feature of poetry. Theory is a characteristic feature of philosophy.

questions.stem: His son is a ______, as he lost his life protecting the lives of people of this country.
questions.explanation: A martyr is someone who dies for a cause or while protecting others. The defining detail is that he lost his life.

questions.stem: Her schoolmates organised a house party for Sara’s birthday, but she does not get excited easily even if you put in a lot of effort and emotion. Sara is ______.
questions.explanation: Placid means calm and not easily excited. Gregarious means sociable, and frenzied means wildly excited.

questions.stem: We bought a new machine to help mother with household chores. The machine can easily be carried anywhere. It is ______.
questions.explanation: Portable means easy to carry. Potable means safe to drink.

questions.stem: Mr Gupta has four wives and twelve children. He is a ______.
questions.explanation: A polygamist has more than one spouse. A bigamist has two; a monogamist has one.

questions.stem: This is Peter’s first press conference. He is anxious because he speaks little. He is ______.
questions.explanation: Reticent means reserved and reluctant to speak. Garrulous is the opposite, and terse means brief without the sense of anxiety.

questions.stem: I cannot stay in the hospital for five minutes because I fear confined places. I have ______.
questions.explanation: Claustrophobia is the fear of enclosed or confined spaces. Agoraphobia is the fear of open or crowded places.

questions.stem: Sheren’s father won an award for a book about his own life. The book is an ______.
questions.explanation: An autobiography is the story of a person’s life written by that person. A biography is written by someone else.

questions.stem: At the ancient palace we saw old manuscripts written by saints, but they were not clear enough to read. They were ______.
questions.explanation: Illegible means impossible to read. Legible and decipherable mean the writing can be read.

questions.stem: I don’t mind talking to him about the project, but he thinks only of himself. He is an ______.
questions.explanation: An egoist is concerned only with himself. A boaster talks about his achievements, which the sentence does not say.

questions.stem: Ancient Greek authors believed that literature should contain a perfect balance between the social and the personal, objectivity and ______, and ______ and emotion.
questions.explanation: The sentence pairs opposites: social with personal, objectivity with subjectivity, and emotion with reason.

questions.stem: If you act ______ at their party, you won’t be asked back; they don’t want spiteful and irritating people at their affairs.
questions.explanation: Splenetic means bad-tempered, spiteful and irritable, which matches the people they do not want.

questions.stem: If you continue to skip classes and fail to complete homework, you will soon find that you have been ______ the university.
questions.explanation: Repeated absence and missed work lead to being dismissed, not invited or merely warned in the strongest reading of “soon find that you have been”.

questions.stem: Asegedech was so abrupt with clients that her supervisor put a letter in her file citing her ______.
questions.explanation: Abrupt treatment of clients is rudeness. The letter cites the fault, not a virtue such as diligence.

questions.stem: Hadas, a passionate woman, agreed to marry a rich, ______ neighbour even though she loved a ______, uneducated man.
questions.explanation: The contrast is a rich, educated neighbour against a poor, uneducated man. The other options repeat the same idea twice.

questions.stem: This professor spent his entire life trying to ______ his students to appreciate the beauty of poetry.
questions.explanation: A teacher trying to bring students to appreciate poetry is encouraging them. Repeal and alienate work against that aim.

questions.stem: Hanan was known for her ______; no one was more ______ than she.
questions.explanation: The second description agrees with the first. Altruism and selfless say the same thing. The other pairs are opposites.

questions.stem: Alemu waited ______ for his turn, relaxing in an easy chair with his eyes closed.
questions.explanation: Relaxing with closed eyes shows he waited calmly, not impatiently or angrily.

questions.stem: People pay little attention to what he says because ______.
questions.explanation: People ignore someone when they cannot trust what he says. Unreliability explains the lack of attention.

questions.stem: Our team scored one goal at the end of the match, but they lost. It was ______.
choices: the final stage of the match
questions.explanation: One late goal was not enough. “Too little too late” means both insufficient and too late to change the result.

questions.stem: “If I had seen her, I would have told her the news” means ______.
choices: he didn’t tell her the news
he told her the news when he saw her
he told her the news when he sees her
he saw her but he didn’t tell her the news
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional about a past that did not happen. He did not see her, so he did not tell her the news.

questions.stem: Despite all his efforts, ______.
questions.explanation: Despite introduces a contrast. Efforts would normally bring success, so the contrasting result is that he was unsuccessful.

questions.stem: I would have met the boss ______.
choices: had I been a bit early
if he is in his office
questions.explanation: “Would have met” needs a past unreal condition. “Had I been a bit early” means he was not early, so he missed the boss.

questions.stem: “Don’t forget to buy Monica a present.” The closest meaning is:
choices: Monica must buy you a gift.
I want you to remember Monica’s address.
I want you to remember to buy Monica a gift.
questions.explanation: The speaker is reminding you to buy the present. The request is about your memory, not Monica buying a gift.

questions.stem: “Feyera speaks Afan Oromo and English.” The closest meaning is:
choices: Feyera speaks to British people on the phone.
questions.explanation: Naming two languages he speaks means he is bilingual. The sentence does not say he is still learning.

questions.stem: “Tinbit is sick and tired of her stepmother.” The closest meaning is:
choices: Tinbit is fed up with her stepmother.
Tinbit needs to take a nap.
Tinbit is sick because she likes her stepmother.
questions.explanation: “Sick and tired of” is an idiom meaning fed up with someone, not a physical illness.

questions.stem: “Emebet is older than Fantu, but younger than Adanu.”
questions.explanation: The order from oldest to youngest is Adanu, Emebet, Fantu. Adanu is the oldest.

questions.stem: “Hagos used to drink a lot of alcohol.”
choices: He no longer drinks a lot of alcohol.
questions.explanation: “Used to” describes a past habit that has stopped. He drank a lot before and does not do so now.

questions.stem: “Daniel can play the kirar and the piano.”
choices: Daniel wants to play the violin instead.
questions.explanation: The kirar and the piano are two instruments, so he plays two.

questions.stem: The 16th century was an age of great ______ exploration.
questions.explanation: The passage opens by calling the 16th century an age of great land exploration.
questions.passage: The 16th century was an age of great land exploration. Magellan lost the favour of the king of Portugal when he became involved in a political entanglement. The Pope divided New World lands between Spain and Portugal according to their location on one side or the other of an imaginary geographical line 50 degrees west of Greenwich that extends in a north and south direction.

questions.stem: Magellan lost the favour of the king of Portugal when he became involved in a political ______.
questions.explanation: The passage says the loss of favour came from a political entanglement.
questions.passage: The 16th century was an age of great land exploration. Magellan lost the favour of the king of Portugal when he became involved in a political entanglement. The Pope divided New World lands between Spain and Portugal according to their location on one side or the other of an imaginary geographical line 50 degrees west of Greenwich that extends in a north and south direction.

questions.stem: The Pope’s imaginary line 50 degrees west of Greenwich extends in a ______ direction.
questions.explanation: A meridian of longitude runs north and south. The passage states that direction directly.
questions.passage: The 16th century was an age of great land exploration. Magellan lost the favour of the king of Portugal when he became involved in a political entanglement. The Pope divided New World lands between Spain and Portugal according to their location on one side or the other of an imaginary geographical line 50 degrees west of Greenwich that extends in a north and south direction.

questions.stem: By leaving Poland and travelling to France to enter the Sorbonne, Marie ______.
questions.explanation: The passage presents that decision as evidence of her intelligence.
questions.passage: Marie Curie showed intelligence by leaving Poland and traveling to France to enter the Sorbonne. Her husband, Pierre Curie, was killed in a street accident involving a horse-drawn wagon. In 1911 Marie Curie received the Nobel Prize in chemistry for isolating radium.

questions.stem: According to the passage, Pierre Curie was killed by ______.
questions.explanation: The passage says Pierre was killed in an accident involving a horse-drawn wagon.
questions.passage: Marie Curie showed intelligence by leaving Poland and traveling to France to enter the Sorbonne. Her husband, Pierre Curie, was killed in a street accident involving a horse-drawn wagon. In 1911 Marie Curie received the Nobel Prize in chemistry for isolating radium.

questions.stem: In 1911 Marie Curie received the Nobel Prize in ______ for isolating radium.
questions.explanation: Her 1903 Nobel Prize was in physics; the 1911 prize, for isolating radium, was in chemistry. The passage states chemistry.
questions.passage: Marie Curie showed intelligence by leaving Poland and traveling to France to enter the Sorbonne. Her husband, Pierre Curie, was killed in a street accident involving a horse-drawn wagon. In 1911 Marie Curie received the Nobel Prize in chemistry for isolating radium.

questions.stem: The total surface area of a cube is 24. What is the volume of the cube?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 faces, so 6a² = 24, a² = 4 and a = 2. The volume is a³ = 8.

questions.stem: A rectangle has perimeter 54 metres. The length-to-width ratio is 5 to 4. What is the length, in metres?
questions.explanation: Let the sides be 5k and 4k. Then 2(5k + 4k) = 54, so 18k = 54 and k = 3. The length is 15.

questions.stem: On a 12-hour clock the time is 11:00. What is the acute angle between the hour and minute hands?
questions.explanation: At 11:00 the minute hand is on 12 and the hour hand is on 11, which is 30° away. The acute angle is 30°.

questions.stem: A is a two-digit number whose last digit is 3, and the difference of its digits is 6. What is A?
questions.explanation: If the units digit is 3, the tens digit must be 9, because |9 − 3| = 6. The number is 93. A negative tens digit is impossible.

questions.stem: If x² − y² = 2 and xy = 4, what is x⁴ + y⁴?
questions.explanation: (x² + y²)² = (x² − y²)² + 4x²y² = 4 + 4(xy)² = 4 + 64 = 68. Then x⁴ + y⁴ = (x² + y²)² − 2x²y² = 68 − 2(16) = 36.

questions.stem: If 25 percent of a number is 1,600, what is 10 percent of the number?
questions.explanation: The number is 1,600 ÷ 0.25 = 6,400. Ten percent of 6,400 is 640.

questions.stem: X can finish a job in 15 days and Y in 20 days. What fraction remains if they work together for 8 days?
questions.explanation: Together they complete 1/15 + 1/20 = 7/60 of the job per day. In 8 days they complete 56/60 = 14/15, so 1/15 remains.

questions.stem: A 10-litre solution is 20% salt. How many litres of an 8% salt solution must be added to make a 12% solution?
questions.explanation: The original salt is 2 litres. If x litres of 8% solution are added, (2 + 0.08x) / (10 + x) = 0.12. Then 2 + 0.08x = 1.2 + 0.12x, so 0.8 = 0.04x and x = 20.

questions.stem: On level ground a building’s shadow is 12 m when a man’s shadow is 0.60 m. The man is 1.80 m tall. How tall is the building, in metres?
questions.explanation: The triangles are similar, so height / shadow is constant. 1.80 / 0.60 = 3, and 3 × 12 = 36.

questions.stem: The last digit of X is 9 and the last digit of Y is 8. Both are two-digit numbers. What is the last digit of X × Y?
questions.explanation: Only the units digits matter: 9 × 8 = 72, which ends in 2.

questions.stem: If n = 9 × 28 × 26, which of the following is NOT an integer?
questions.explanation: n = 9 × 28 × 26 = 2³ × 3² × 7 × 13. Dividing by 32 = 2⁵ needs two more factors of 2 than n has, so n/32 is not an integer. The other divisors all divide n.

questions.stem: If 0 < x < y < 1, which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Both numbers are positive and y is larger than x, so y/x is greater than 1. Their product and difference are each less than 1.

questions.stem: Three times the third of three consecutive odd integers is 3 more than twice the sum of the first and the second. What is the sum of the three integers?
questions.explanation: Let the integers be n, n+2 and n+4. Then 3(n+4) = 3 + 2(n + n+2), so 3n + 12 = 4n + 7 and n = 5. The integers are 5, 7 and 9, and their sum is 21.

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has perimeter 30 m. What is its area, in m²?
questions.explanation: Each side is 10 m. Area = (√3 / 4) × side² = (√3 / 4) × 100 = 25√3.

questions.stem: The sides of a triangle are in the ratio 3 : 5 : 6, and the perimeter is 70 m. What is the longest side, in metres?
questions.explanation: The sides are 3k, 5k and 6k. Then 14k = 70, so k = 5 and the longest side is 30.

questions.stem: The price of 2 ties and 3 shirts is Birr 2,800. The same amount buys 1 tie and 5 shirts. What is the price of 1 tie and 1 shirt?
questions.explanation: 2t + 3s = t + 5s = 2,800, so t = 2s. Then 4s + 3s = 2,800, s = 400 and t = 800. One of each costs 1,200.

Quantity M is (526)² − (525)². Quantity N is 210. Which is true?
What is the least value of x for which (2x + 1)(x − 2) = 0?
questions.explanation: The solutions are x = −1/2 and x = 2. The smaller value is −1/2.

questions.stem: If a − b = p, what is a² − 2ab + b²?
questions.explanation: a² − 2ab + b² is (a − b)², which equals p². Note that p(a − b) is also p², so D is numerically the same; the direct simplified form is p².

questions.stem: If n = 3, what is 2^(2n) + 1?
questions.explanation: 2n = 6, so 2^6 + 1 = 64 + 1 = 65. The nearby traps are 2^6 = 64 and 2^7 + 1 = 129.

questions.stem: A priest asks, “Do you speak to the devil and follow his biddings?” The parishioner says yes. The priest replies, “You must be lying. Nobody who is in league with the devil tells the truth.” Why is the priest’s behaviour paradoxical?
choices: His behaviour followed religious law, but he accused the parishioner of violating it.
He relied on the parishioner’s answer in order to reject that answer.
He accused the parishioner, then later changed his story.
He asked about the devil but does not believe the devil exists.
questions.explanation: The priest uses the “yes” as evidence, then says anyone in league with the devil would lie. He depends on an answer that his own rule says cannot be trusted.

questions.stem: Turkey’s GDP rose 8.5% in 2011, but inflation was high and much of its banking system is part-owned by Eurozone banks. As the single currency falters, that dependency raises questions about the stability of Turkish growth. Which conclusion follows?
choices: Turkish banks are European-owned mainly to help Turkey join the European Union.
The Turkish economy was stagnant in 2011.
European ownership was chosen to add variety to the market.
There are concerns that Turkey’s development may falter after 2011.
questions.explanation: The passage itself says the dependency raises questions about the stability of growth. It does not give a reason for the ownership, and it reports rapid growth rather than stagnation.

questions.stem: Ahmed lives in a big apartment. Abay lives in a small apartment. There are no big apartments in Hawassa. Small apartments have one bedroom. Which must be true?
questions.explanation: Abay lives in a small apartment, and every small apartment has one bedroom. Ahmed’s big apartment cannot be in Hawassa, but Abay’s home is not located.

questions.stem: About 55% of people in poverty in Ethiopia are government employees, and this is expected to reach 60% by 2025. Also, 25% of people in poverty are not government employees because they are unfit to work through age or disability. Which follows?
choices: There are equal numbers of people in poverty and in government employment.
20% of people in poverty are not government employees, but they are fit to work.
The number of people in poverty will rise.
questions.explanation: If 55% are government employees, 45% are not. Of that 45%, 25 percentage points are unfit, leaving 20% who are not government employees and are fit to work.

questions.stem: Cleo is a good dog. Clona is a bull. Good dogs are fast and keep the house safe. Bulls do not make noise. Which must be true?
questions.explanation: Cleo is a good dog, and every good dog is fast. Nothing says bulls are fast or that Cleo is quiet.

questions.stem: Technology companies that make tablets and smartphones should invest in making them more intuitive for elderly people. This group has not been reached and could benefit greatly. The argument depends on which assumption?
choices: Elderly people would want to buy tablets and smartphones.
Technology companies are already investing in this area.
Apps for elderly people are already in development.
Elderly people do not like new technology.
questions.explanation: The recommendation only makes sense if elderly people would actually want the devices. If they would not buy them, the untapped market disappears.

questions.stem: Good education is the lifeblood of the country. We need to keep class sizes from being too large by building new schools. Which is assumed?
choices: Young pupils are a vital part of the country.
Class sizes are too large and must be reduced.
People work better in smaller classes.
questions.explanation: Calling for new schools so that classes will not be too large assumes that classes are currently too large. The argument does not discuss building costs.

questions.stem: Kaliti Flour Factory has 180 employees. Factories with fewer than 200 employees are classified as small manufacturers. Therefore:
choices: Kaliti Flour Factory is a small manufacturer.
Kaliti Flour Factory has sizable employees.
Kaliti Flour Factory is a big manufacturer.
Kaliti Flour Factory is categorized as a small manufacturer.
questions.explanation: 180 is less than 200, so the factory meets the definition of a small manufacturer. D says the same thing in different words.

questions.stem: Not everyone with a car has a licence, and not everyone with a licence owns a car. Everyone with a licence has taken the driving test. Everyone who drives on the road has a licence. Ahmed drives on the road. Therefore:
choices: Ahmed has taken his driving test.
Some drivers on the road have taken the driving test.
questions.explanation: Ahmed drives, so he has a licence, and everyone with a licence has taken the test. A and D also follow; the direct conclusion about Ahmed is that he has taken the test. He need not own a car.

questions.stem: There are no politicians who are not party members. There are no appointees who are not politicians. Which must be true?
choices: Any party member is also an appointee.
There is no party member who is not a politician.
questions.explanation: All appointees are politicians, and all politicians are party members, so all appointees are party members. The reverse claims do not follow.

questions.stem: All university teachers can teach in secondary schools. University teachers trained in Ethiopia can teach in Ethiopian universities, but not in Kenya. Which follows?
choices: All secondary teachers can teach at university.
A university teacher trained in Ethiopia can teach anywhere.
A university teacher trained in Ethiopia can teach at a secondary school or a university in Ethiopia.
All university teachers in Kenya can teach in Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: A university teacher trained in Ethiopia is a university teacher, so he can teach in secondary school, and the second sentence allows him to teach in an Ethiopian university.

questions.stem: Loft insulation saves on heating bills, but leaving the heating on with the windows open wastes energy. Wasting energy raises bills. Zeberga has loft insulation but regularly leaves the heating on with the windows open.
choices: Zeberga’s loft insulation does not work.
questions.explanation: Leaving the heating on with the windows open is given as wasting energy, and Zeberga does that. The insulation does not cancel that stated waste.

questions.stem: At Addis Ababa University everyone works 8 hours, but people start at different times. Tigist started at 9 AM, at least one hour after everyone else. Whoever leaves last must lock up. Which must be true?
choices: Tigist started one hour before everyone else.
Everyone in the office has to lock up.
Everyone else started at 8 AM or earlier.
Everyone must start work at 8 AM.
questions.explanation: Tigist’s 9 AM start was at least one hour after every other person, so nobody else started after 8 AM. Only the last person to leave locks up.

questions.stem: All birds have beaks, and all sparrows are birds. Therefore:
choices: Almost all sparrows must have beaks.
questions.explanation: Sparrows are birds and every bird has a beak, so every sparrow has a beak. “Some” is weaker but also true.

questions.stem: The family doctor said he would perform a blood test today. The patient concludes, “I know I will feel pain today.” The argument depends on which assumption?
choices: The doctor will have trouble finding a vein.
Using a needle always causes the patient pain.
The doctor will have to try several needles.
This patient has felt pain at this doctor’s office before.
questions.explanation: A blood test leads to pain only if the needle used for the test is assumed to cause pain. Past visits and difficult veins are not required.

questions.stem: THIGH : LEG
questions.explanation: The thigh is part of the leg. The palm is part of the hand. A thumb is a kind of finger, not part of a finger.

questions.stem: DILIGENCE : SUCCESS
questions.explanation: Diligence can produce success, just as victory can produce ecstasy. The other pairs are closer to synonyms.

questions.stem: FISH : SARDINE
questions.explanation: A sardine is a kind of fish. A chicken is a kind of fowl.

questions.stem: PARENT : CHILD
questions.explanation: A parent produces a child. A couple produces offspring. The other pairs are family relations of a different kind.

questions.stem: DERMATOLOGY : SKIN
questions.explanation: Dermatology is the study of skin. Histology is the study of tissue.

questions.stem: PERCEPTIBLE
questions.explanation: Perceptible means able to be noticed or seen. Noticeable is the closest meaning. Visible is also acceptable.

questions.stem: OFFENCE
questions.explanation: In this vocabulary set the choices contrast a fault with its opposite. Offence here is paired with immorality, the general moral wrong; cruelty is only one kind of offence.

questions.stem: SERENE
questions.explanation: Serene means calm and quiet. Noisy is an antonym, and sedentary means sitting still.

questions.stem: PROHIBIT
questions.explanation: To prohibit is to forbid or block something. Deter means to discourage, which is weaker than a prohibition.

questions.stem: There are several reasons why school uniforms must be ______ for all students.
questions.explanation: The natural completion is that uniforms must be worn. Mandatory repeats the idea of “must,” and sought or found does not fit a rule about uniforms.

questions.stem: Computer ______ can be defined as the excessive or compulsive use of the computer which persists despite serious negative ______.
questions.explanation: Compulsive use that continues despite harm is addiction, and the harm is described as negative consequences.

questions.stem: Almost every aspect of modern life has been ______ through the convenience provided by technology.
questions.explanation: Convenience that touches almost every aspect of life is an improvement. Disjointed would be a loss of convenience.

questions.stem: Unlike human beings, the computer ______ repetitive calculations without getting tired or ______.
questions.explanation: Computers perform calculations, and the human failure they avoid is becoming bored or tired.

questions.stem: In order to succeed in class, students need to ______ the resources available to them throughout their studies.
questions.explanation: Success comes from using the resources that are already available. Utilize means to put them to use.

questions.stem: It is certain that advertising is an everyday ______ of our lives.
questions.explanation: Something present every day is a feature of daily life. A forecast or a demand is not what advertising itself is.

questions.stem: In the strictest sense, the ______ of a material would produce a ______ supply of the original.
questions.explanation: Recycling returns used material as a fresh supply of the original kind. Discarding reduces supply rather than producing it.

questions.stem: Obesity is a medical condition in which excess body fat has ______ to the extent that it may harm health.
questions.explanation: The medical definition of obesity is excess body fat that has accumulated enough to affect health.

questions.stem: She always gets up early ______ be late for work.
questions.explanation: She gets up early for the purpose of avoiding lateness. “In order not to be late” is the complete infinitive of purpose.

questions.stem: She asked me if I ______ the film before.
questions.explanation: The reporting verb “asked” is past, so the earlier experience is past perfect: had seen.

questions.stem: The committee chose to postpone the meeting rather than ______ it that day.
questions.explanation: After “rather than,” the gerund matches the structure used here: postpone the meeting rather than having it.

questions.stem: We all left the place ______ as soon as we heard the blast.
questions.explanation: The blank modifies the verb “left,” so it needs the adverb hurriedly.

questions.stem: She didn’t want to stop and talk to me ______.
choices: in spite of her busy schedule
questions.explanation: Being busy explains why she would not stop. “In spite of her busy schedule” would mean she stopped despite being busy.

questions.stem: According to the text, which statement is true?
choices: World Champion is a title held for life.
Grandmaster is a higher title than World Champion.
World Champion is a higher title than Grandmaster.
The title World Champion is awarded by FIDE.
questions.explanation: The passage says Grandmaster is the highest title apart from World Champion, so World Champion ranks higher. Only the Grandmaster title is said to be held for life and awarded by FIDE.
questions.passage: The title Grandmaster is awarded to chess players by the world chess organisation FIDE. Apart from World Champion, Grandmaster is the highest title a chess player can attain. Once achieved, the title is held for life.

questions.stem: The passage implies you should pay attention to Charles Morris because:
choices: His predictions have come true once already.
The U.S. is becoming more energy independent.
His first book was a best seller.
questions.explanation: The reason to trust the new forecast is that his earlier warning about the 2008 recession came true. Being published, by itself, is not the point of the passage.
questions.passage: Six years ago, lawyer-banker-scholar Charles Morris wrote a prophetic book, Two Trillion Dollar Meltdown, that foresaw the 2008 Great Recession before it hit America and the world. Now Morris has reversed course and sees good times ahead. His forthcoming book, Comeback, predicts that growing U.S. energy independence will bring a rise in American manufacturing and jobs.

questions.stem: In 2000 E.C. a jacket cost Birr p. The price rose 20% in each of the next years, but in 2003 it fell by 10%. What was the total percentage increase from 2000 to 2003?
questions.explanation: The multipliers are 1.20 for 2001, 1.20 for 2002 and 0.90 for 2003. 1.2 × 1.2 × 0.9 = 1.296, which is a 29.6% increase.

questions.stem: A class has 29 students, 15 of them girls. The girls average 42 kg and the boys average 45 kg. A new student of 54 kg joins. What is the new average weight, in kg?
questions.explanation: There are 14 boys. Total weight is 15×42 + 14×45 = 630 + 630 = 1,260. Adding 54 gives 1,314 kg for 30 students, and 1,314 / 30 = 43.8.

questions.stem: Quantity M is (526)² − (525)². Quantity N is 210.
questions.explanation: The difference of squares is (526 − 525)(526 + 525) = 1,051, which is greater than 210.

questions.stem: What is the least value of x for which (2x + 1)(x − 2) = 0?
questions.explanation: Set each factor equal to zero: x = −1/2 or x = 2. The least is −1/2.

questions.stem: Region R is where y ≤ x + 2 and y ≥ x². For a point (x, y) in R, what is the maximum of 2y − x?
questions.explanation: Because the coefficient of y is positive, use the largest allowed y, which is x + 2. Then 2y − x = x + 4. The region also needs x + 2 ≥ x², so x is between −1 and 2. The maximum of x + 4 on that interval is 6, at x = 2, y = 4.

questions.stem: Scores and frequencies: 2 (1), 5 (4), 6 (2), 8 (2), 10 (1). Which statement is true?
choices: The median is the average of the mode and the mean.
The mode is greater than the mean and the median.
The mean, mode and median are equal.
The mean is the average of the mode and the median.

choices: two sides of the same coin

questions.explanation: The passage uses both descriptions, so the complete answer is both.
questions.passage:
A duty is an obligation. It is something we owe to others as social beings when we live together. We must let others live with us. My right of living implies my duty to my fellow men to allow them the same conditions of life. In fact, rights and duties are co-related. What is a right in regard to one is a duty in regard to others. Rights and duties are two sides of the same coin. We should always observe them from the standpoint of others. Thus they are duties. Moral duty is more effective than the legal. A moral duty is that which is laid upon people on moral grounds. It is my moral duty to help the poor because I am a member of society.

I must try to create conditions which contribute to the welfare of humanity. Similarly, I owe a duty to my parents — to be obedient and respectful to them. This duty originates from the sense of responsibility which is directly related to our conscience. So this maxim is concerned with a moral duty which a person should owe without legal bondage.

Sense of duty is paramount for the proper development of civilization. Hypocrisy and diplomacy are quite reverse to the sense of duty. Hypocrisy involves wickedness; duty involves sincerity and faithfulness.

questions.stem: An appropriate title for the passage would be:
questions.explanation: The passage’s own phrase is the miracle by which timid people, facing danger that must be met, suddenly find courage.
questions.passage: When we are suddenly confronted with any terrible danger, the change of nature we undergo is equally great. In some cases fear paralyses us. Like animals, we stand still, powerless to move a step in fright or to lift a hand in defence of our lives, and sometimes we are seized with panic and again act more like the inferior animals than rational beings. On the other hand, frequently in cases of sudden extreme peril, which cannot be escaped by fright and must be instantly faced, even the most timid men at once, as if by miracle, become possessed of the necessary courage, sharp quick apprehension and swift decision. This is a miracle very common in nature. Man and the inferior animals alike, when confronted with almost certain death, "gather resolution from despair", but there can really be no trace of so debilitating a feeling in the person fighting, or prepared to fight, for dear life. At such times the mind is clearer than it has ever been; the nerves are steel; there is nothing felt but a wonderful strength and daring. Looking back at certain perilous moments in my own life, I remember them with a kind of joy, not that there was any joyful excitement then, but because they brought me a new experience — a new nature, as it were — and lifted me for a time above myself.

The United States has already chosen service over domination.
A new president must be decisive.
The previous administration had been irresponsible.
questions.explanation: Choosing not to dominate assumes domination is possible. Otherwise the contrast between serving and dominating would not be a real choice.

Mathematics matters less than other abilities.
Women and men should be equally capable.
Women might be more capable than men.
Women tend to conform to social expectations.

Other ingredients in dry bread can neutralise the inactive virus.
Many cancer patients said they ate dry bread.
Ten percent of the rural population uses dry bread.
No medicine can kill the inactive virus.
questions.explanation: If other ingredients neutralise the virus, finding it in bread does not mean eating the bread exposes cells to an active cancer risk.

Retaining dignity never involves taking liberty from others.
There is always the possibility of a dignified intrusion.
questions.explanation: If dignified behaviour requires no intrusion, and the writer says avoiding intrusion is impossible, then dignity cannot be kept without that intrusion.

questions.stem: SCHOLAR : IGNORANT

questions.stem: REDUNDANT
questions.explanation: Redundant means more than is needed. Insufficient means not enough.

questions.stem: EMPATHY
questions.explanation: Empathy is feeling for other people. The opposite is a lack of that feeling.

questions.stem: UBIQUITOUS
questions.explanation: Ubiquitous means found everywhere. Rare is the opposite.

questions.stem: MITIGATE
questions.explanation: To mitigate is to make something less severe. To worsen is the opposite.

questions.explanation: Timetables use the simple present. Her plane arrives at three.

questions.explanation: “More and more” describes a change in progress, so the present continuous is getting is used.

questions.stem: If I ______ money, I would purchase it now.
questions.explanation: This is a second conditional: if + past simple, then would + verb. The past form is had.

questions.stem: She is looking for accommodation ______ in a flat or a shared house.
questions.explanation: Either … or presents the two choices.

questions.stem: Maryam, accompanied by her brother, ______ at the party last night.

questions.stem: The newly imposed rules sound very ______.

questions.stem: The passive equivalent of “We gave the police some information” is:

The police were given some information.
Some information was given to the police.
Both “The police were given some information” and “Some information was given to the police.”

questions.stem: “Belay would have bought a new car if he had been a rich man” means:

Belay was rich, but he didn’t buy a new car.

questions.stem: The ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 5, and there are 24 boys. How many girls are there?
questions.explanation: 3 parts are 24, so 1 part is 8. Girls are 5 × 8 = 40.

questions.stem: Using the same class, 24 boys and girls in the ratio 3 : 5, how many students are there in total?
questions.explanation: Boys are 24 and girls are 40, so the class has 64 students.

questions.stem: A mother is 4 times as old as her child. In 8 years she will be twice as old as the child. How old is the mother now?
questions.explanation: Let the child be c. Then 4c + 8 = 2(c + 8), so c = 4 and the mother is 16.

questions.stem: Three workers finish a task in 12 days. How many days will six workers need at the same rate?
questions.explanation: The job is 36 worker-days. Six workers finish it in 6 days.

questions.stem: What is 25% of 80?
questions.explanation: A quarter of 80 is 20.

questions.stem: Of 30 people, 18 have an engineering degree, 12 have a management degree, and 7 have both. How many have neither?
questions.explanation: People with at least one degree: 18 + 12 − 7 = 23. Neither: 30 − 23 = 7.

questions.stem: What is the least common multiple of 12 and 15?
questions.explanation: 12 = 2² × 3 and 15 = 3 × 5, so the LCM is 2² × 3 × 5 = 60.

questions.stem: A man washes a car in 12 minutes. His son takes twice as long. How long do they take together?
questions.explanation: Their rates are 1/12 and 1/24, which add to 1/8. Together they need 8 minutes.

questions.stem: Split 50 into two parts whose reciprocals add to 1/12.
questions.explanation: If the parts are a and 50 − a, then 1/a + 1/(50 − a) = 1/12. That gives a(50 − a) = 600, so the parts are 20 and 30.

questions.stem: The difference of the squares of two consecutive even numbers is 84. What is their sum?
questions.explanation: If the numbers are n and n + 2, then (n + 2)² − n² = 4n + 4 = 84, so n = 20. The numbers are 20 and 22, and their sum is 42.

questions.stem: The 10th term of an arithmetic progression is 84 and the common difference is 8. What is the first term?
questions.explanation: The 10th term is the first term plus 9 differences: a + 72 = 84, so a = 12.

questions.stem: The difference between the squares of two consecutive odd integers is always divisible by:
questions.explanation: Consecutive odd integers are 2k − 1 and 2k + 1. The difference of their squares is 8k, which is always divisible by 8.

questions.stem: How many numbers between 100 and 200 are divisible by 3?
questions.explanation: The numbers run from 102 to 198. That is (198 − 102) / 3 + 1 = 33 numbers.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the roots of x² − 7x + 10 = 0?
questions.explanation: For x² − sx + p = 0, the sum of the roots is s. Here that sum is 7.

questions.stem: Simplify √98 − √50.
questions.explanation: √98 = 7√2 and √50 = 5√2. The difference is 2√2.

questions.stem: A container holds 50 litres of milk. Three times in a row, 5 litres are removed and replaced with water. How much milk is left?
questions.explanation: Each replacement leaves 45/50 of the milk. After three times, 50 × (0.9)³ = 36.45 litres remain.

questions.stem: The digits of a two-digit number multiply to 8. Adding 18 reverses the digits. What is the number?
questions.explanation: If the number is 10a + b, then ab = 8 and 10a + b + 18 = 10b + a, so b = a + 2. Then a(a + 2) = 8, and a = 2. The number is 24. Check: 24 + 18 = 42.

questions.stem: If x + y = 24, what is the maximum value of xy?
questions.explanation: The product is largest when the numbers are equal. Each is 12, and 12 × 12 = 144.

questions.stem: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 9 : 7 : 4. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: The ratio has 20 parts and the angles sum to 180°, so each part is 9°. The largest angle is 9 × 9 = 81°.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 7, 10 and 5. What type is it?
questions.explanation: All three sides are different, so it is scalene. It is not right-angled, because 5² + 7² is not 10².

questions.stem: What is the area of a circle with radius 6 cm?
questions.explanation: Area is πr² = 36π.

questions.stem: A rectangle has perimeter 48 cm and its length is twice its width. What is the width?
questions.explanation: 2(2w + w) = 48, so 6w = 48 and the width is 8 cm.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a cube with side 4 cm?
questions.explanation: Volume is 4³ = 64 cm³.

questions.stem: A cone has base radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume is (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π × 9 × 4 = 12π.

questions.stem: A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed is distance divided by time: 180 / 3 = 60 mph.

questions.stem: A 5 by 12 rectangle is inscribed in a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: The diagonal is the diameter. √(5² + 12²) = 13, so the radius is 6.5.

questions.stem: How many positive divisors does 1420 have?
questions.explanation: 1420 = 2² × 5 × 71. The number of divisors is (2 + 1) × (1 + 1) × (1 + 1) = 12.

questions.stem: What is the value of 16^(log₄ 5)?
If CAT is written as 3120, how is DOG written?
questions.explanation: Each letter is its place in the alphabet: C=3, A=1, T=20. D=4, O=15, G=7, so DOG is 4157.

questions.stem: Find the missing number: 2, 6, 12, 20, ?, 42.
questions.explanation: The gaps are +4, +6, +8, +10, +12. The missing term is 20 + 10 = 30, and 30 + 12 = 42.

questions.stem: How is F related to J?
questions.explanation: J is E’s father, and F is married to E. F is J’s daughter-in-law.
questions.passage: A family has six members: E, F, G, H, I and J. E is married to F. G is the son of E. H is the brother of G. I is the sister of G. J is the father of E.

questions.stem: How is I related to H?
questions.explanation: I and H are both children of E, and I is female, so I is H’s sister.
questions.passage: A family has six members: E, F, G, H, I and J. E is married to F. G is the son of E. H is the brother of G. I is the sister of G. J is the father of E.

questions.stem: E is the brother of F, F is the sister of G, and G is the father of H. How is H related to E?
questions.explanation: E and G are siblings. H is G’s child, so H is E’s nephew or niece.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: 3, 5, 9, 13, 17.
questions.explanation: 3, 5, 13 and 17 are prime. 9 = 3 × 3, so it is the odd one out.

questions.stem: All apples are fruits. Some fruits are sweet. Which follows?
choices: Only “some sweet things are apples” follows.
questions.explanation: The sweet fruits might not be apples, so neither conclusion is forced.

questions.stem: A man walks 10 km north, turns left and walks 5 km, then turns right and walks 10 km. Where is he from the start?
questions.explanation: Left from north is west. After 5 km west he turns right, so he faces north again and walks 10 km. He is 20 km north and 5 km west, which is north-west.

questions.stem: All roses are flowers, and some flowers fade quickly. Which is true?
choices: None of these must be true.
questions.explanation: The flowers that fade quickly might not include any roses. None of the stronger claims must be true.

questions.stem: In a Venn diagram, elements that belong to both set E and set F are the:
choices: symmetric difference of E and F
questions.explanation: The overlap of two sets is their intersection.

questions.stem: What comes next: 1A, 2B, 3C, 4D, …?
questions.explanation: The number increases by 1 and the letter moves forward one place. Next is 5E.

questions.stem: The minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is between 2 and 3. What time is it?
questions.explanation: The minute hand on 6 means 30 minutes. The hour hand between 2 and 3 means 2:30.

questions.stem: Rearranging the letters of IMARONA gives the name of:
questions.explanation: IMARONA rearranges to ROMANIA, which is a country.

questions.stem: What comes next: AB, BC, CD, …?
questions.explanation: Each pair starts with the second letter of the previous pair. After CD comes DE.

questions.stem: A father is twice as old as his son. Five years ago the father was three times as old as his son. What are their ages now, son and father?
questions.explanation: Let the son be s. Then 2s − 5 = 3(s − 5), so s = 10 and the father is 20.

questions.stem: Four years ago E was twice as old as F. E is 40 now. How old is F?
questions.explanation: Four years ago E was 36, so F was 18 then. F is 22 now.

questions.stem: A box has 3 red, 2 blue and 5 green balls. What is the probability of picking a red ball?
questions.explanation: There are 10 balls and 3 are red, so the probability is 3/10.

questions.stem: If CAT is written as DBU, how is DOG written?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward one place. D-O-G becomes E-P-H.

questions.stem: Some E is F, and all F are G. Which must be true?
questions.explanation: The F’s that are also E must be G, so some E is G. The same overlap means some G is E.

questions.stem: A man faces east. He turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise. Which way does he face?
questions.explanation: A clockwise quarter-turn from east faces him south. A half-turn anticlockwise from south faces him north.

questions.stem: In a class of 40, 30 study maths, 25 study science, and 20 study both. How many study only maths?
questions.explanation: Only maths is 30 − 20 = 10.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: Apple, banana and cherry are fruits. A carrot is a vegetable.

questions.stem: All cats are mammals. Some mammals are not dogs. Therefore some cats are not dogs.
questions.explanation: The mammals that are not dogs might not be cats. The premises do not force the conclusion.

questions.stem: A clock shows 3:15. What is the angle between the hands?
questions.explanation: At 3:00 the hands are 90° apart. In 15 minutes the hour hand moves 7.5°, so the angle is 90 − 7.5 = 7.5°.

questions.stem: Some books are pens, and some pens are not pencils. Which must be true?
questions.explanation: “Some books are pens” is the same fact as “some pens are books.” Nothing is said that forces a link between books and pencils.

questions.stem: How many students had taken only mathematics?
questions.explanation: Remove the overlaps from 15. Only maths and chemistry is 2, only maths and physics is 6, and all three is 3. Only mathematics is 15 − 2 − 6 − 3 = 4.
questions.passage: In a survey of 25 students, 15 had taken mathematics, 12 physics and 11 chemistry. Five had taken mathematics and chemistry, 9 had taken mathematics and physics, 4 had taken physics and chemistry, and 3 had taken all three.

questions.stem: How many students had taken only chemistry?
questions.explanation: Only chemistry is 11 − 2 − 1 − 3 = 5.
questions.passage: In a survey of 25 students, 15 had taken mathematics, 12 physics and 11 chemistry. Five had taken mathematics and chemistry, 9 had taken mathematics and physics, 4 had taken physics and chemistry, and 3 had taken all three.

questions.stem: How many students had taken only physics?
questions.explanation: Only physics is 12 − 6 − 1 − 3 = 2.
questions.passage: In a survey of 25 students, 15 had taken mathematics, 12 physics and 11 chemistry. Five had taken mathematics and chemistry, 9 had taken mathematics and physics, 4 had taken physics and chemistry, and 3 had taken all three.

questions.stem: How many students had taken exactly one course?
questions.explanation: Only maths, physics and chemistry are 4, 2 and 5. That is 11 students.
questions.passage: In a survey of 25 students, 15 had taken mathematics, 12 physics and 11 chemistry. Five had taken mathematics and chemistry, 9 had taken mathematics and physics, 4 had taken physics and chemistry, and 3 had taken all three.

questions.stem: How many students had taken at least one of the three courses?
questions.explanation: Add the only-one regions (11), the exactly-two regions (9) and the centre (3). That is 23.
questions.passage: In a survey of 25 students, 15 had taken mathematics, 12 physics and 11 chemistry. Five had taken mathematics and chemistry, 9 had taken mathematics and physics, 4 had taken physics and chemistry, and 3 had taken all three.

questions.stem: How many students had taken none of the courses?
questions.explanation: 25 students were surveyed and 23 took at least one course, so 2 took none.
questions.passage: In a survey of 25 students, 15 had taken mathematics, 12 physics and 11 chemistry. Five had taken mathematics and chemistry, 9 had taken mathematics and physics, 4 had taken physics and chemistry, and 3 had taken all three.

questions.stem: How many students had taken exactly two of the three courses?
questions.explanation: Exactly two means the pairwise overlaps without the centre: (5 − 3) + (9 − 3) + (4 − 3) = 2 + 6 + 1 = 9.
questions.passage: In a survey of 25 students, 15 had taken mathematics, 12 physics and 11 chemistry. Five had taken mathematics and chemistry, 9 had taken mathematics and physics, 4 had taken physics and chemistry, and 3 had taken all three.

questions.stem: What was the percentage increase in Branch A’s sales from September to October?
questions.explanation: The increase is 30 on a base of 150, which is 20%.
questions.passage: September and October sales, in birr: Branch A 150 then 180; Branch B 200 then 250; Branch C 120 then 100.

questions.stem: What is the ratio of Branch A’s two-month total to Branch B’s two-month total?
questions.explanation: A totals 330 and B totals 450. Divide by 30 to get 11 : 15.

exams.summary: Verbal, quantitative, statistics and analytical items from a second university model and public NGAT practice.

questions.stem: RESTIVE
questions.explanation: Restive means restless or hard to keep still.

questions.stem: CRAVEN
questions.explanation: Craven means cowardly.

questions.stem: PERFIDY
questions.explanation: Perfidy is treachery. The opposite is loyalty.

questions.stem: EFFICACY
questions.explanation: Efficacy means effectiveness. The opposite is inefficiency.

questions.stem: CARPENTER : SAW
questions.explanation: A carpenter works with a saw. A reaper works with a sickle.

questions.stem: MENDACITY : HONESTY
questions.explanation: Mendacity is the opposite of honesty. Courage is the opposite of cravenness.

questions.stem: Anas, Umar and I ______ going.
questions.explanation: The subject is three people, so the verb is are.

questions.stem: If I ______ time, I would have purchased it yesterday.
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional about yesterday. The if-clause needs the past perfect: had had.

questions.stem: Please try and do the assignment as ______ as you can.
questions.explanation: Well is the adverb that describes how the work is done. Good is an adjective.

questions.stem: He should have taken more time ______ his essay.
questions.explanation: “Take time to edit” uses the infinitive.

questions.stem: “It’s good news that Rashid passed his first-year exams, ______? Let’s hope he’s ______ next year, too.”
questions.explanation: The tag for “it’s” is “isn’t it.” After “he’s,” the word that fits is the adjective successful.

questions.stem: ______ sure you adhere to the ethical procedures when carrying ______ your research project.
questions.explanation: The sentence is an instruction, so it starts with the imperative Make. “Carry out” means perform.

questions.stem: Which word is most like “altered” in “Have you altered the introduction?”
questions.explanation: To alter a text is to amend it.

questions.stem: Which word is most like “assume” in “I assume the tutors can help”?
questions.explanation: To assume is to suppose something is true.

questions.stem: Which phrase uses “intense” in the usual way?
questions.explanation: Pain is commonly described as intense. The other pairings are not.

questions.stem: Which phrase uses “relief” in the usual way?
questions.explanation: The set phrase is “a sigh of relief.”

questions.stem: Is that ______ “8” or ______ “B”? I can’t read it.
questions.explanation: “Eight” starts with a vowel sound, so it takes an. “Bee” starts with a consonant sound, so it takes a.

questions.stem: We huddled together for warmth ______ the blankets.
questions.explanation: They were under the blankets, so the preposition is beneath.

questions.stem: There were very ______ people on the beach, so nobody saw the child drowning.
questions.explanation: People is a plural countable noun. “Very few people” is the correct phrase.

questions.stem: Would you like ______ bread?
questions.explanation: Bread is measured as a loaf.

questions.stem: There is ______ butter left. We need to buy ______ more.
questions.explanation: Butter is uncountable, so the quantity word is little, and the extra amount is some.

questions.stem: Which sentence about glittering is correct?
choices: All that glitters is not gold.
All these glitters is not gold.
All that glitters are not gold.
questions.explanation: “That” is singular here, so the verb is is. The proverb is “All that glitters is not gold.”

questions.stem: She has been ______ to music all day.
questions.explanation: “Has been” is followed by the present participle: listening.

questions.stem: When I came to this city, I ______ anyone.
questions.explanation: “When I came” is a finished past time, so the verb is the simple past didn’t know.

questions.stem: Which sentence about being ready is correct?
choices: One should keep oneself ready for an emergency.
One should kept himself or herself ready for an emergency.
One should be keeping himself ready for an emergency.
One should keep himself to herself ready for an emergency.
questions.explanation: “One” is followed by oneself, and the verb after should is the base form keep.

questions.stem: Did you just ______ me a liar?
questions.explanation: After did, the verb stays in the base form: call.

questions.stem: Those newspapers ______ in a big truck.
questions.explanation: The newspapers receive the action, and the subject is plural, so the verb is are delivered.

questions.stem: If a + 2b = x and a − 2b = y, which expression equals ab?
questions.explanation: Adding the equations gives a = (x + y) / 2. Subtracting gives b = (x − y) / 4. Their product is (x² − y²) / 8.

questions.stem: Two integers add to 42 and differ by 22. What is the greater integer?
questions.explanation: Adding the two facts gives 2x = 64, so the greater integer is 32.

questions.stem: If a² = 17, what is (a + 1)(a − 1)?
Abebe, Beletu and Omar paid 490 dollars for a laptop. Abebe paid 50 dollars more than Beletu, and Beletu paid twice what Omar paid. How much did Abebe pay?
questions.explanation: Let Omar pay o. Then Beletu pays 2o and Abebe pays 2o + 50. The total is 5o + 50 = 490, so o = 88 and Abebe pays 226.

questions.stem: An office has 30 trainees and one team lead. The average age of all 31 people is 27. Leaving out the team lead lowers the average by 1 year. How old is the team lead?
questions.explanation: The whole group sums to 31 × 27 = 837. The 30 trainees average 26, so they sum to 780. The lead is 837 − 780 = 57.

questions.stem: Nineteen friends paid 120 dollars each for movie tickets. The twentieth friend paid 38 dollars more than the average paid by all twenty. What did the twenty friends pay altogether?
questions.explanation: Let the total be T. Then T = 19 × 120 + T/20 + 38. So (19/20)T = 2318 and T = 2440.

questions.stem: A means ×, B means ÷, C means +, and D means −. What is 306 B 34 A 7 D 7 C 5?
questions.explanation: The expression is 306 ÷ 34 × 7 − 7 + 5. Division and multiplication come first: 9 × 7 = 63, then 63 − 7 + 5 = 61.

questions.stem: What is the sum of all the positive factors of 28?
questions.explanation: The factors are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 and 28. They add to 56.

questions.stem: In an election, 20% of 4,850 votes were invalid. One candidate received 35% of the valid votes. How many valid votes did the other candidate receive?
questions.explanation: Valid votes are 80% of 4850, which is 3880. The other candidate received 65% of those: 0.65 × 3880 = 2522.

questions.stem: A, B and C share 669 so that A : B = 17 : 27 and B : C = 2 : 5. What is C’s share?
questions.explanation: Make B the same in both ratios: A : B : C = 34 : 54 : 135. Those parts sum to 223, and 669 / 223 = 3, so C gets 135 × 3 = 405.

questions.stem: A team finishes a job in 20 days. With the team leader, the same job takes 15 days. How long would the leader take alone?
questions.explanation: The leader’s rate is 1/15 − 1/20 = 1/60. Alone, the leader needs 60 days.

questions.stem: B is 5/2 times A. A is what percent of B?
Five children were born 3 years apart. Their ages sum to 50. How old is the youngest?
questions.explanation: The ages are x, x + 3, x + 6, x + 9 and x + 12. They sum to 5x + 30 = 50, so x = 4.

questions.stem: If log 2 = 0.3010, what is log₅ 512, to three decimal places?
Sending 10 students from room A to room B makes the rooms equal. Sending 20 from B to A makes A twice B. How many students are in room A at the start?
questions.explanation: Let A start with a and B with b. Then a − 10 = b + 10, and a + 20 = 2(b − 20). Solving gives a = 100 and b = 80.

questions.stem: The price of 10 chairs equals the price of 4 tables. Fifteen chairs and 2 tables cost 4000 birr. What do 12 chairs and 3 tables cost?
questions.explanation: Ten chairs match four tables, so one table costs the same as 2.5 chairs. Then 15 chairs + 2 tables = 20 chairs = 4000, so a chair is 200 and a table is 500. Twelve chairs and three tables cost 3900.

questions.stem: Each side of a rectangle is increased by 20%. By what percent does the area increase?
questions.explanation: The new area is 1.2 × 1.2 = 1.44 times the old area, which is an increase of 44%.

questions.stem: A train at 60 km/h crosses a pole in 9 seconds. How long is the train?
questions.explanation: 60 km/h is 50/3 metres per second. In 9 seconds the train covers 150 metres, which is its own length.

questions.stem: From 8:00 in the morning to 2:00 in the afternoon, through how many degrees does the hour hand turn?
questions.explanation: That interval is 6 hours. The hour hand moves 30° per hour, so it turns 180°.

questions.stem: A square of side 2 m has its corners cut off so that the result is a regular octagon. What is the side of the octagon?
questions.explanation: If a length x is cut from each end of a side, the remaining side is 2 − 2x and each new edge is x√2. Setting them equal gives x = 2 − √2, and the octagon side is 2(√2 − 1), which equals 2 / (√2 + 1).

questions.stem: A ladder leans against a wall with its top 8 m above the ground. Moving the foot 2 m farther from the wall brings the top down to the foot of the wall. How long is the ladder?
questions.explanation: Let the length be L. At first the foot is L − 2 from the wall, so (L − 2)² + 8² = L². That gives L = 17.

questions.stem: A 6 m by 2 m pool is surrounded by a walkway of uniform width. The walkway has area 48 m². How wide is it?
questions.explanation: If the width is w, then (6 + 2w)(2 + 2w) − 12 = 48. This simplifies to w² + 4w − 12 = 0, so w = 2.

questions.stem: The mean of a distribution is 48 more than the mode, and the median is 12. What is the mean? Use mode = 3 × median − 2 × mean.
questions.explanation: Mode = 3 × 12 − 2 × mean = 36 − 2 × mean. Then mean − mode = 3 × mean − 36 = 48, so the mean is 28.

questions.stem: On which day is the History exam?
questions.explanation: Two exams after Biology puts Biology on Thursday, so English, two days before it, is on Monday. Mathematics is after Biology and not on Friday, so it is on Saturday, and Physics is on Tuesday. Friday is then History.
questions.passage: Six exams — English, Mathematics, History, Physics, Chemistry and Biology — run on Monday through Saturday, one each day. Physics is not on Wednesday, and Mathematics is not on Wednesday. Exactly two exams come after Biology. Exactly two exams come between Biology and English. Chemistry is not on Friday, and Mathematics is not on Friday. Exactly three exams come between Physics and Mathematics, and Mathematics comes after Biology.

questions.stem: In a rain-affected match, Team A beat Team B by 50 runs under the Duckworth–Lewis rule. Which inference follows?
choices: Only this: Duckworth–Lewis is a rule used to decide a rain-affected match.
Only this: Team B batted first.
questions.explanation: The statement uses the rule to settle a rain-affected match, so the first inference follows. A win by runs means the winner batted first, so Team B did not bat first.

questions.stem: Garry skipped one number while counting from 1 to 10. It was even, greater than 3 and less than 9, and upside down it looks like a different digit. Which number was it?
questions.explanation: The even numbers in that range are 4, 6 and 8. Turned upside down, 6 looks like 9.

questions.stem: Which of these does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Goggles, spectacles and bifocals are worn over the eyes. An optical reader is a device.

questions.stem: 139 is related to 228, and 122 is related to 211. What is related to 2 in the same way?
questions.explanation: Each second number is 89 more than the first. 2 + 89 = 91.

questions.stem: On which day is English taught?
questions.explanation: Tuesday already has Chemistry and Geography. History cannot share Monday with Maths without making a third class, so History and English are both on Wednesday.
